evals.name: module-layer-design
evals.prompt: I'm adding a small new feature to DevDigest (Fastify + Drizzle + Postgres, TypeScript): automatically flag PRs that touch files with no test coverage (an 'untested-touch' rule) and persist that flag per PR so the UI can show a badge. Design the module from scratch: what files/classes/interfaces do I need, where does each one live, and how do I wire it into the DI container (server/src/platform/container.ts)? Sketch the file layout and key signatures — no need for full implementations, just enough to see the shape and the dependency direction.
evals.expected_output: A layered module (domain/application/adapters) where the rule/entity logic has zero framework imports, the use case depends on a port interface (not a concrete repository class), the concrete Postgres repository + a row<->domain mapper live in the adapter layer, wiring happens once in container.ts, and a mock adapter is mentioned for testing the use case without a real DB.

assertions.text: Proposes explicit domain/application/adapters separation for the new module rather than one flat file or service
The domain layer (rule/entity) has no Drizzle/Fastify/HTTP or other framework/infra import
The application/use-case class depends on a port/interface for persistence, not a concrete adapter class
Recommends wiring the concrete adapter into the use case at the composition root (container.ts), not inside the use case itself
Shows or mentions a mapper translating between the DB row shape and the domain entity, kept at the adapter boundary
Mentions adding a mock/test double for the new port so the use case can be unit-tested without a real DB

evals.name: domain-importing-infra
evals.expected_output: Flags the domain entity importing the Drizzle table/schema directly (outward dependency from domain to infra) and flags the toRow() row-mapping method living inside the domain class. Fix: the entity depends only on plain/domain types, and mapping to the Drizzle insert/select shape moves to a separate adapter-level mapper (e.g. invoice.mapper.ts), matching the pattern in server/src/adapters/.

assertions.text: Identifies that the domain entity imports the Drizzle table/schema directly, violating inward-only dependency direction
Identifies that the toRow() row-mapping method lives inside the domain entity and should move to an adapter-level mapper
Proposes a concrete fix: the entity depends only on primitive/domain types, and mapping to $inferInsert/$inferSelect happens in a separate mapper
Provides corrected code implementing the fix, not just a description of the problem

evals.name: use-case-instantiates-adapter
evals.expected_output: Flags the use case constructing the concrete PostgresInvoiceRepository itself (and importing it directly) instead of depending on a port/interface injected via the constructor. Fix: the use case takes a repository port interface as a constructor parameter; the concrete Postgres adapter is instantiated once and wired in at the composition root (container.ts), matching the pattern in server/src/platform/container.ts.

assertions.text: Identifies that the use case constructs the concrete PostgresInvoiceRepository itself instead of receiving it via constructor injection
Explains the concrete downside: the use case can't be unit-tested without a real DB / breaks DI
Proposes the use case depend on a port/interface type, injected via the constructor
Proposes wiring the concrete adapter at the composition root (container.ts) rather than inside the use case

evals.name: controller-bypasses-use-case
evals.expected_output: Flags the route handler calling the repository directly instead of going through an application/use-case layer, and flags returning the raw DB row from GET instead of a mapped response. Critically, notes that going straight from route to repository means the pay endpoint updates the status column directly and never calls Invoice.markPaid() — so paying a void invoice is not actually prevented, even though the domain rule exists. Fix: introduce use cases (e.g. GetInvoiceUseCase / PayInvoiceUseCase) that load the domain entity, call markPaid(), and persist through a mapper.

assertions.text: Identifies that the route handler calls the repository directly instead of going through an application/use-case layer
Identifies that the void-invoice invariant (Invoice.markPaid()) is bypassed because the route updates the row directly, i.e. flags the resulting reachable bug, not just the structural smell
Identifies that the raw DB row is returned directly from the GET endpoint instead of a mapped DTO/domain-shaped response
Proposes concrete restructuring: a use case that the route calls, with domain rule enforcement and mapping at the boundary

evals.name: sibling-module-coupling
evals.comparison: skill-version (old SKILL.md snapshot vs. new SKILL.md with added Step 6 on sibling-module coupling) — not with_skill/without_skill
evals.expected_output: Flags the notifications module reaching directly into billing's adapter-layer concrete repository class (PostgresInvoiceRepository) and instantiating it itself, instead of going through billing's own public surface (a shared port, an exported use case, or an HTTP call). Explains that this couples notifications to billing's storage internals across a module boundary. Proposes a fix that depends on something billing intentionally exposes (a port/interface billing publishes, or a container-level shared dependency) rather than importing billing/adapters/db/* from outside billing.

assertions.text: Identifies that NotificationService imports/instantiates billing's concrete PostgresInvoiceRepository directly across the module boundary (modules/notifications -> modules/billing/adapters)
Explains the downside: notifications is now coupled to billing's storage internals and can't be tested or changed independently of billing's concrete adapter
Proposes a fix that goes through billing's own public surface (a port billing exposes, an exported use case, or an HTTP call) instead of importing modules/billing/adapters/db/* from outside billing
Provides a concrete corrected structure/code sketch, not just a description of the problem
